run.notes: FIRST SERVE ON THIS RIG. Measured on the rig's own hardware slot: EC2 g6.2xlarge (1x NVIDIA L4, Ada SM 8.9), us-east-1d, spot. Benchmark was driven ON THE INSTANCE against localhost, so no WAN latency is in TTFT/ITL. This run exists to be the RUNTIME CONTROL for gpu-jax-g6-2b (48.3-48.5 tok/s, 2026-08-28, same chip and same checkpoint) -- and unlike the T4G pair, BOTH SIDES ARE STOCK: no Triton patch, no hand-reduced tiles, no from-source build.

model.architecture_notes: Heterogeneous head dims (sliding_attention 256 / full_attention 512) force TRITON_ATTN: vLLM logs 'FA4 not available, forcing TRITON_ATTN backend'. IT RAN UNPATCHED ON ADA -- no OutOfResources, which is the question this rig was built to answer. 9.8 GiB of weights are resident, but the roofline proves not all of it is streamed per token (see notes[]).

software.backend: TRITON_ATTN (forced by vLLM; VLLM_ATTENTION_BACKEND deliberately unset)

probes.observed: 4096-in/128-out ran at both conc=1 and conc=8; 16384 max_model_len not exercised to its limit.

memory.notes: vLLM saw 22.04 GiB free of 23034 MiB (22.49 GiB) reported by nvidia-smi. Workspace = 0.22 GiB peak activation + 0.09 GiB CUDA graphs. KV MEASURED AT 9622 B/token (9.40 KiB), roughly HALF the ~18 KiB/token this rig's CLAUDE.md carried as arithmetic. 1,076,849 resident KV tokens = 65.73x max concurrency at 16384 ctx, so KV is nowhere near binding and fp8 KV remains unnecessary here.

startup.notes: From corrected-bootstrap start to /health 200. Image pull 105 s; container start +109 s; weights download 37.6 s; model load 40.8 s; engine init 124.03 s (79.32 s compile). EXCLUDES the first launch, which failed outright -- see issues[].

cost.notes: Whole-instance spot rate on a single-GPU size, so rate_per_chip_hour is the instance rate. No comparisons[] entry is offered against the JAX sibling: it ran on g6.xlarge-class capacity at a different spot price, so a $/token difference would be a PRICE artifact, not a runtime result. Compare tok/s, not dollars.

issues.summary: vllm/vllm-openai:v0.27.2rc0 -- the tag this rig shipped with -- IS NOT A PUBLISHED IMAGE TAG. cloud-init died at 'failed to resolve reference ... not found'. It is the G5g sibling's VLLM_REF, a GIT ref that rig compiled from source, copied into an IMAGE TAG field at the fork. Published releases are v0.27.0, v0.27.1, v0.28.0 -- there is no v0.27.2 of any kind. Fixed by moving to v0.28.0, which is above the model's per_layer_config floor.

test_image_is_at_or_above_the_measured_vllm_floor did not catch the above: it forbids the known-bad tags but never asserts the tag RESOLVES. A guard that only blocklists cannot catch a value that is in no list.

verify_gpu_arch reports 'SM 8.9 is in the arch list' but sm_89 is NOT literally present -- torch was built for sm_75/80/86/90/100/120. Ada runs the sm_86 cubins by same-major-version binary compatibility. The matmul (which passed) is the real evidence; the message overstates what it checked.

notes: ROOFLINE ON STREAMED, NOT RESIDENT, BYTES -- AND DECODE IS NOT BANDWIDTH-BOUND. E2B streams 3.382 GB/token (transformer matmuls 2.576 + tied LM head 0.805); the 4.698 GB PLE table is an indexed GATHER, not a stream (derivation and cross-check in the monorepo MODELS.md, 'Resident is not streamed'). At 46.09 tok/s that is 155.9 GB/s of the L4's 300 GB/s = 52% MBU, so the bandwidth-implied ceiling is 88.7 tok/s and this run sits at 52% of it. Independent confirmation that resident is the wrong denominator: 46.09 tok/s x 9.8 GiB resident would demand 485 GB/s, which the 300 GB/s bus makes physically impossible. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RUNTIME COMPARISON: vLLM (46.09) and JAX (48.3-48.5) are BOTH at roughly half the memory roofline, so the ~5% gap between them is an overhead / kernel-launch difference at B=1, NOT a memory-system one. Matches the T4G finding that no runtime tested there was bandwidth-bound at B=1.

RUNTIME COMPARISON, the reason this rig exists: vLLM 46.09 tok/s single-stream vs gpu-jax-g6-2b 48.3-48.5 tok/s (2026-08-28), same L4, same checkpoint. vLLM is ~5% slower at concurrency 1. BOTH SIDES STOCK -- this is the first clean runtime comparison in this tree.
vLLM's advantage is batching, not single-stream: 46.09 -> 360.17 tok/s from concurrency 1 to 8 is 7.8x on 8x the load (98% scaling efficiency). TPOT stays flat, 19.85 -> 21.71 ms.

SILICON COMPARISON, same runtime and same harness (vllm bench serve): gpu-vllm-g5g-2b/benchmarks/runs/2026-08-14-rust-frontend-g5g on a g5g.4xlarge (T4G, Turing) measured c=1 ~31.8 tok/s (TPOT 31.44 ms), c=4 ~97 tok/s, c=8 168.33 tok/s. This L4 run: c=1 46.09, c=4 175.83, c=8 360.17 -- 1.45x / 1.81x / 2.14x. The gap WIDENS with concurrency, which is the Ada/Turing difference plus a much larger KV pool (9.65 GiB vs the T4G's 15360 MiB total device memory). NOTE the T4G side ran with hand-reduced Triton tiles; this side is stock. Do NOT compare against the loose 43.1/44.24 tok/s figures -- CLAUDE.md records that neither is a benchmark.
Context cost is modest: 1024 -> 4096 input costs 6% of single-stream decode (46.09 -> 43.30) but 42% at concurrency 8 (360.17 -> 207.83), where prefill competes with decode.
Ada's ~99 KiB of per-block shared memory cleared Triton's ~96 KiB tile UNPATCHED. The G5g sibling's local patch to triton_unified_attention.py is NOT needed here and must not be ported in.
